text:
Ava: FYI started a reserved GPU pool provisioning in eu-west1 and the bootstrap kept failing with healthcheck 503s on the edge proxy

infra-bot: [ALERT] pool-gpu-reserve-12 failed: backend healthcheck mismatch (target-group: tg-edge-proxy-eu-west1)

Jon: seeing same. pods are Ready but register -> failing HC from ALB. kubectl describe svc/proxy says externalTrafficPolicy: Local and endpoints present.

Priya: can you paste the ALB target health failure reason? usually 'connection refused' vs 'timeout' tells if it's network or app.

Ava: ALB target description from aws: 
""
TargetHealth: { State: unhealthy, Reason: HttpCodeMismatch, Description: 'Health checks failed: 503' }
""

Marta: 503 from HC often means ALB can reach the node but the node is dropping traffic or rewriting source port and NACL/SG denies return. Did you check node security groups and subnet NACLs?

Jon: ran packet capture on node host: `sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 'port 8080'` - see SYN from ALB IP -> SYN/ACK from node but then RST from some infra IP. weird.

Priya: pulling network acl for the subnet now: `aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-xx`

Priya: found a DENY rule with ruleNumber 1005 that's broad: `egress DENY 0.0.0.0/0 ports 32768-65535` (looks like a previous lockdown to prevent ephemeral leaks).

Marta: aha. ALB healthchecks are from ELB/ALB source ports ephemeral -> target ephemeral ephemeral return path needs ephemeral allowed in NACL. Order matters (lower ruleNumber takes precedence). If that DENY is before allow rules it's an implicit deny trap.

Jon: so ALB -> node: dest 8080, source ephemeral port (like 54321). Node responds from 8080 -> dest 54321. NACL egress blocking 32768-65535 will drop that response if it's evaluated on the subnet return path. Exactly matches the tcpdump (SYN/ACK then RST seen from gateway).

Ava: confirmed the rule: ruleNumber 1005 deny egress 32768-65535. It was added during tighter egress lockdown last quarter. It was intended for NAT subnets only but got applied to edge subnets too.

ops-oncall: priority plan: 1) add an allow egress rule for 32768-60999 with smaller ruleNumber (e.g., 900) on edge subnet NACL; 2) add SG outbound allow for ALB ephemeral range if missing; 3) roll HC canary after 5m. Who takes 1?

Jon: I'll patch the NACL to insert allow rule at 900 (temporary rollback). running: `aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0abc --rule-number 900 --protocol -1 --rule-action allow --egress --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range From=32768,To=60999`

Priya: note: NACL port-range 32768-60999 is the recommended ephemeral for our kernels; older rule used 65535 which is too broad. good to limit. Also make sure the rule number is lower than the deny (so it hits first).

Marta: after Jon patches, I'll run `aws elbv2 describe-target-health` and `kubectl get pods -o wide` then try curl from the ALB IP using a curl instance in same AZ.

Jon: patched NACL rule 900 -> allow 32768-60999 egress. confirmed with describe-network-acls shows allow at 900 then deny at 1005.

Ava: re-registering targets... waiting for healthy status

infra-bot: [UPDATE] tg-edge-proxy-eu-west1 target x.x.x.x changed status to healthy (after 45s).

Priya: canary looks good. ALB HC now returns 200 consistently. rolling the reserved GPU pool again should succeed.

Jon: rolling pool again... provisioning succeeded, healthchecks steady.

Ava: root cause summary: an overly-broad DENY egress NACL (rule 1005) applied to edge subnets blocked ephemeral return ports used by ALB healthchecks. NACL order meant deny beat allow until we inserted a lower-numbered allow rule.

Marta: follow-ups: 1) move allow rule into IaC (terraform change) with proper ordering and limited port range; 2) audit other subnets for same accidental DENY; 3) add a runbook note about ALB->node ephemeral port behavior. I'll create PR for the Terraform change.

Jon: added terraform TODO and a quickgrep to find `egress deny` rules in our infra repo.

Ava: thanks all. adding postmortem tag and scheduling 1hr retro tomorrow to tighten change control on network lockdowns. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: assigning follow-ups: Marta (TF PR), Jon (audit grep + quick fix), Priya (runbook entry). I'll open tickets and assign.
